title: How Medical Marijuana Works
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss medical marijuana: the list of conditions it is used for, the Venice Beach "Cush Doctor" sign, the federal government's shifting stance (the DEA, U.S. attorneys, Obama-era raids versus his 2009 memo), California's research funding and Senate Bill 420 ID cards and caregiver rules, THC and the endocannabinoid system, synthetic THC (Marinol) versus the cannabis extract Sativex, state medical marijuana laws (Oregon, Washington, and others), dispensary crackdowns in Los Angeles and a RAND crime study, and public opinion polls. They also cover Brownie Mary and close with listener mail.
topics: Stuff You Should Know listener mail

segments.title: Opening banter and list of conditions
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck introduce medical marijuana and read the list of conditions it is claimed to help, including the sign outside the Cush Doctor in Venice Beach, California.

segments.title: Federal government and state conflict
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the tension between medical research supporting marijuana and federal opposition, including the federal program from 1970, states' rights, federal raids on dispensaries, and Obama's 2009 memo.
topics: federal vs state law on marijuana

segments.title: Recent federal crackdown and raid numbers
segments.summary: Discussion of the reversal under the DEA and U.S. attorneys, the number of raids under Obama, criticism from advocates, and the Colorado and Rhode Island responses.

segments.title: California research and federal restrictions
segments.summary: California received about nine million dollars for medical marijuana research starting around 2000, but federal rules on sourcing and inspections made study difficult. Federal agencies also threatened firearms dealers over sales to marijuana users, and dispensaries shifted to cash-only operations.

segments.title: How THC and the endocannabinoid system work
segments.summary: THC is the cannabinoid that makes people high and also holds the medicinal properties. The body produces its own endocannabinoids that bind to receptors and regulate pain, anxiety, appetite, mood and memory. The hosts also mention a mouse study on tumors.

segments.title: Synthetic THC (Marinol) versus whole-plant extracts
segments.summary: Synthetic THC is sold as Marinol, a prescription pill. Critics say it lacks parts of the natural plant. Sativex is a cannabis extract sprayed under the tongue, legal in several countries and in US trials. The DEA compares Marinol to morphine versus opium.

segments.title: State laws, Oregon and Washington, and California's Senate Bill 420
segments.summary: Eighteen states plus D.C. have medical marijuana laws, with Oregon and Washington allowing large possession amounts. Doctors cannot legally prescribe marijuana, so they issue recommendations. California's Senate Bill 420 created ID cards and possession limits, and counties such as Humboldt expanded them. Caregiver rules are also discussed.

segments.title: Dispensary crackdowns, caregivers, and public opinion
segments.summary: Discussion of why the caregiver protections became unclear, the Los Angeles closures of hundreds of dispensaries, the RAND Corporation crime study, polling showing support for medical marijuana, and the VA recommending cannabis for PTSD.

segments.title: Listener mail from Matt in Minneapolis
segments.summary: The hosts read a humorous listener email about a supposed Mayan prince in Iowa, a street gang, butterfly anatomy, and an honorary gang membership. They invite more listener mail through Twitter, Facebook and email.
